properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...Eastern Randolph County in southwestern Georgia...
Terrell County in southwestern Georgia...

* WHEN...Until 800 AM EDT.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas.
Water over roadways.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 507 AM EDT, Doppler radar indicated heavy rain due to
thunderstorms. Minor flooding is ongoing or expected to begin
shortly in the advisory area. Between 2 and 3 inches of rain have
fallen.
- Additional rainfall amounts of 1 to 3 inches are expected over
the area. This additional rain will result in minor flooding.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Dawson, Bronwood, Parrott, Yeomans, Oakville, Graves, Dawson
Municipal A/P, Bridges Crossroad and Chambliss.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

Please report observed flooding to local emergency services or law
enforcement and request they pass this information to the National
Weather Service when you can do so safely.

properties.description:
FFWTAE

The National Weather Service in Tallahassee has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
East Central Dale County in southeastern Alabama...
Henry County in southeastern Alabama...
Clay County in southwestern Georgia...
Quitman County in southwestern Georgia...
Randolph County in southwestern Georgia...

* Until 745 AM EDT /645 AM CDT/.

of rain have fallen. The expected rainfall rate is 1.5 to 4 inches

possible in the warned area. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected
to begin shortly.

highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas.

Abbeville, Fort Gaines, Cuthbert, Shellman, Newville, Bellville,

properties.description:
SMWTAE

The National Weather Service in Tallahassee has issued a

* Special Marine Warning for...
Coastal Waters from Mexico Beach to Apalachicola out 20 NM...
Coastal waters from Okaloosa-Walton County Line to Mexico Beach out
20 NM...
St. Andrews Bay Waterways...
Waters from Okaloosa-Walton County Line to Mexico Beach from 20 to
60 NM...

* Until 530 AM CDT.

* At 325 AM CDT, a severe thunderstorm capable of producing
waterspouts was located 11 nm east of Okaloosa Deep Water Reef, or
20 nm south of Santa Rosa Beach, moving northeast at 10 knots.

HAZARD...Waterspouts and wind gusts 34 knots or greater.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Waterspouts can quickly form and capsize boats...damage
vessels...and create suddenly higher waves. Make sure all
on board are in a secure location and wearing life
jackets. Expect wind gusts in excess of 34
knots...suddenly higher waves...frequent lightning...and
heavy downpours. Make sure all on board are wearing life
jackets.

* Locations impacted include...
Mexico Beach, Port St. Joe, Panama City Beach, Laguna Beach,
Apalachicola, Cape San Blas, Sandestin, Miramar Beach, and Santa
Rosa Beach.
properties.instruction:
Move to safe harbor until hazardous weather passes.

Thunderstorms can produce sudden waterspouts. Waterspouts can easily
overturn boats and create locally hazardous seas. Seek safe harbor
immediately.

properties.areaDesc: Yuma
properties.headline: Extreme Heat Watch issued October 5 at 12:06AM MST until October 8 at 8:00PM MST by NWS Phoenix AZ
properties.description:
* WHAT...Dangerously hot conditions possible. Afternoon temperatures
104 to 107. Major Heat Risk.

* WHERE...Yuma.

* WHEN...From Wednesday morning through Thursday evening.

* IMPACTS...Heat related illnesses increase significantly during
extreme heat events. Overexposure can cause heat cramps and heat
exhaustion to develop and, without intervention, can lead to heat
stroke.
properties.instruction:
An Extreme Heat Watch means that a period of very hot temperatures,
even by local standards, may occur. Actions should be taken to lessen
the impact of the extreme heat.

Take extra precautions if you work or spend time outside. When
possible, reschedule strenuous activities to early morning or
evening. Know the signs and symptoms of heat exhaustion and heat
stroke. Wear lightweight and loose-fitting clothing when possible and
drink plenty of water.

To reduce risk during outdoor work, the Occupational Safety and
Health Administration recommends scheduling frequent rest breaks in
shaded or air conditioned environments. Anyone overcome by heat
should be moved to a cool and shaded location. Heat stroke is an
emergency! Call 9 1 1.

Public cooling shelters are available in some areas. Consult county
officials for more details.

properties.headline: Heat Advisory issued October 5 at 2:25AM AST until October 5 at 3:00PM AST by NWS San Juan PR
properties.description:
* WHAT...This level of heat affects most individuals sensitive to
heat, especially those without effective cooling and/or adequate
hydration.

* WHERE...Puerto Rico and U.S. Virgin Islands.

* WHEN...From 10 AM this morning to 3 PM AST this afternoon.

* IMPACTS...High temperatures or elevated heat indices can worsen
symptoms in people with chronic conditions. They can also increase
the risk of heat-related illness among individuals sensitive to
heat with inadequate cooling or hydration. These risks are highest
across coastal areas, lowlands, interior valleys, and urban zones.
properties.instruction:
Drink plenty of fluids, stay in an air-conditioned room, stay out of
the sun, and check up on relatives and neighbors.

Take extra precautions when outside. Wear lightweight and loose
fitting clothing. Try to limit strenuous activities to early morning
or evening. Take action when you see symptoms of heat exhaustion and
heat stroke.

properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued October 5 at 2:20AM EDT until October 5 at 5:15AM EDT by NWS Tallahassee FL
properties.description:
FFWTAE

The National Weather Service in Tallahassee has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Central Coffee County in southeastern Alabama...
Northwestern Dale County in southeastern Alabama...

* Until 415 AM CDT.

* At 120 AM CDT, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing
heavy rain across the warned area. Between 1 and 3 inches of rain
have fallen. Additional rainfall amounts up to 2 inches are
possible in the warned area. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected
to begin shortly.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Elba, Fort Rucker, Enterprise, Ozark, New Brockton, Ariton, Lee,

temperatures in a matter of minutes.

properties.areaDesc: Northern Copper Valley; Western Copper Valley; Central Copper Valley; Ernestine; Southern Copper Valley
properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued October 4 at 7:50PM AKDT by NWS Anchorage AK
properties.description:
Areas of locally dense fog will persist along portions of the
Glenn and Richardson Highways, especially from Glennallen west to
Mendeltna, this evening through early Monday morning.

Periods of a wintry mix of precipitation are also expected across
the Copper River Basin through Monday morning. With temperatures
around freezing for most locations, any precipitation may fall as
a mix of rain, snow, and freezing drizzle. Little to no
significant snow and ice accumulation is expected. However, the
combination of falling precipitation and temperatures around
freezing may result in slippery road conditions and patchy black
ice. The precipitation and fog is expected to taper off by early
to mid Monday morning.

Motorists are urged to slow down and use caution while traveling.
For the latest road conditions call 5 1 1 or visit
511.alaska.gov.

NWSheadline: AREAS OF DENSE FOG ALONG WITH PERIODS OF A WINTRY MIX OF RAIN, SNOW, AND FREEZING DRIZZLE FOR THE CENTRAL COPPER RIVER BASIN THROUGH MONDAY MORNING

properties.areaDesc: Catalina and Santa Barbara Islands; Ventura County Beaches; Malibu Coast; Los Angeles County Beaches
properties.headline: Beach Hazards Statement issued October 4 at 7:33PM PDT until October 8 at 8:00PM PDT by NWS Los Angeles/Oxnard CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...Dangerous rip currents and breaking waves are expected
due to elevated surf of 3 to 6 feet. Abnormally high morning and
evening tides of 6.5 to 7 ft are expected.

* WHERE...Catalina and Santa Barbara Islands, Ventura County
Beaches, Malibu Coast and Los Angeles County Beaches. Most
susceptible areas will be Long Beach and Avalon Harbor Tuesday
and Wednesday. Then, Malibu to Ventura Wednesday through
Friday.

* WHEN...From Tuesday afternoon through Thursday evening.

* IMPACTS...There is an increased risk of ocean drowning. Rip
currents can pull swimmers and surfers out to sea. Waves can
wash people off beaches and rocks, and capsize small boats
nearshore. Moderate flooding of sea water is possibly over
some vulnerable low-lying coastal areas, especially around the
morning and evening high tides, including over beach parking
lots, bike paths, and harbor walkways. Moderate beach erosion
is possible to likely.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...There is a moderate chance that an
upgrade to Coastal Flood Advisory and/or High Surf Advisory
will be needed. These products will likely need to be extended
into the weekend.
properties.instruction:
Remain out of the water due to hazardous swimming conditions, or
stay near occupied lifeguard towers. Rock jetties can be deadly
in such conditions, stay off the rocks.

properties.areaDesc: Majuro Coastal Waters
properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued October 5 at 10:24AM ChST by NWS Tiyan GU
properties.description:
UPDATED to account for Invest 94W becoming TD 27W.

...HEAVY SHOWERS, GUSTY WINDS, AND CHOPPY SEAS LIKELY THE NEXT FEW
DAYS ACROSS THE NORTHERN MARSHALL ISLANDS DOWN TO MAJURO...

A developing disturbance known as Invest 94W by the Joint Typhoon
Warning Center (JTWC) is located about 140 miles southwest of
Utirik. Scatterometry data indicates 15 to 20 kt winds near
Kwajalein, Ebadon, Ujae, Bikini, and Rongelap, with winds up to 25 kt
near heavier showers. TD 27W will be generally slow to move,
remaining over the northern Marshall Islands through Tuesday night.
Scattered to numerous showers and isolated thunderstorms may lead to
locally heavy rainfall and flooding. Through Friday, 4 to 6 inches of
rain with locally higher amounts are possible.

Gusty winds and elevated, choppy seas will make marine conditions
difficult. Residents may need to reconsider plans for inter-island
boating as the week continues.

27W will continue to develop near Kwajalein over the next day or
two, so residents in the northern Republic of Marshall Islands (RMI)
should monitor the forecast for the next several days.

For more information on Invest 94W please see the Significant Tropical
Weather Advisory from the Joint Typhoon Warning Center under WMO
header ABPW10 PGTW. Also keep up to date with the latest information
from your local emergency management agency.

properties.areaDesc: Matagorda Islands; Brazoria Islands; Galveston Island; Bolivar Peninsula
properties.headline: Rip Current Statement issued October 4 at 3:39PM CDT until October 5 at 1:00PM CDT by NWS Houston/Galveston TX
properties.description:
* WHAT...Dangerous rip currents.

* WHERE...Gulf-facing beaches, including the Matagorda
Peninsula, Brazoria County beaches, Galveston Island and the
Bolivar Peninsula.

* WHEN...Through Monday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away
from shore into deeper water.
properties.instruction:
Swim near a lifeguard and away from rocks, jetties, and piers. If
caught in a rip current, relax and float. Don't swim against the
current. If able, swim in a direction following the shoreline. If

properties.areaDesc: South Walton; Coastal Bay; Coastal Gulf; Coastal Franklin
properties.headline: Rip Current Statement issued October 4 at 2:14AM EDT until October 6 at 5:00AM EDT by NWS Tallahassee FL
properties.description:
* WHAT...Dangerous rip currents.

* WHERE...Walton and Bay County Beaches.

* WHEN...Through late Monday night.

* IMPACTS...Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away
from shore into deeper water.
properties.instruction:
Swim near a lifeguard. If caught in a rip current, relax and
float. Don't swim against the current. If able, swim in a
direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the
shore and call or wave for help.
